- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% for the next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or volatile, model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–4% for the next 7–14 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.2 → +0.5), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment momentum as a filter — if sentiment flips, adjust forecast direction accordingly.
